messages.content: You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Choose a parameter (e.g., temperature, pressure, relative humidity…). Consider a table consisting of two columns: month and measured values of the chosen parameter. In the column of measured values, find the highest value. Once found, read the corresponding month in the other column. Return this month as the output.If the highest value appears in multiple cells, return all the corresponding months as the output.
On which month of the year Y was the highest value of the examined parameter recorded for station Z?
The highest value was recorded on month X of year Y.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Choose a parameter (e.g., temperature, pressure, relative humidity…). Consider a table consisting of one column: the measured values of the chosen parameter. First, find the highest value, then the lowest. After finding them, calculate the difference using the formula: maximum value - minimum value = result. Return this result as the output. If the highest and lowest values appear multiple times, consider each only once.
By how much do the maximum and minimum values of the examined parameter differ in year Y for station Z?
The maximum and minimum values differ by X units.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Consider the parameter temperature. Consider a table consisting of one column: the measured temperature values. Search and count all the measured values below 0°C. Return the total number of values below 0°C as the result.
How many times did the temperature drop below 0°C at station Z in year Y?
The temperature dropped below 0°C X times in year Y.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Choose a parameter (e.g., temperature, pressure, relative humidity…). Consider a table consisting of one column: the measured values of the chosen parameter. Count how many measured values are present in the table. Sum all the measured values in the table. Apply the following formula: total sum of values / number of values = result. Return this result as the output.
What is the average annual value of the examined parameter in year Y for station Z?
The average annual value of the parameter in year Y is X.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Choose a parameter (e.g., temperature, pressure, relative humidity…). Consider a table consisting of one column: the measured values of the chosen parameter. Count how many times each measured value appears in the table. The value that appears the most is the result.
What was the most frequent value (mode) of the examined parameter in year Y for station Z?
The most frequent value of the parameter in year Y was X.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Choose a parameter (e.g., temperature, pressure, relative humidity…). Consider a table consisting of one column: the measured values of the chosen parameter.Count how many measured values are present in the table. Obtain the number of missing measurements using the formula:(48 × 366) – number of measured values = result Where: 48 = number of measurements per day (1 every 30 minutes) and 366 = number of days in year Y. Return this result as the output.
In year Y, how many measurements of the examined parameter were not recorded due to technical issues with station Z?
The number of measurements not recorded due to technical issues was X in year Y.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Choose a parameter (e.g., temperature, pressure, relative humidity…). Consider a table consisting of two columns: month and measured values of the chosen parameter. In the column of measured values, find the lowest value. Once found, read the corresponding month in the other column. Return this month as the output. If the lowest value appears in multiple cells, return all the corresponding months as the output.
On which month of the year Y was the lowest value of the examined parameter recorded for station Z?
The lowest value was recorded on month X of year Y.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Choose a parameter (e.g., temperature, pressure, relative humidity…). For 2023: consider a table consisting of one column: the measured values of the chosen parameter. Count how many measured values are in the table.Sum all the values. Apply the formula:total sum / number of values = result 1. For 2024: repeat the same procedure to obtain result 2. Then apply the formula: result 2 – result 1 = result. Return this result as the output.
By how much has the average value of the examined parameter changed over the last two years (2023 and 2024) for station Z?
The average value changed by X units between 2023 and 2024.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Choose a parameter (e.g., temperature, pressure, relative humidity…). Consider a table consisting of one column: the measured values of the chosen parameter. Sort the measured values in ascending order. Count the number of measured values. If the number of values is odd, calculate the median using this method: total values / 2 = number point five Round number point five up to the next integer = result 1. Find the value in the result 1 position of the sorted list. That value is the output. If the number of values is even: total values / 2 = result 2. Find the values at positions result 2 and result 2 + 1 in the sorted list. Sum the two values and divide by 2. That result is the median and the output.
When ordering the dataset of the examined parameter in ascending order, what is the median value for year Y for station Z?
The median value of the parameter in year Y is X.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Choose a parameter (e.g., temperature, pressure, relative humidity…). Consider a table consisting of two columns: month and measured values of the chosen parameter. For each month, find the maximum and minimum values of the chosen parameter and calculate their difference: maximum – minimum = result. The month with the highest result represents the greatest discrepancy and is the required output.
In which month of year Y does the examined parameter show the greatest discrepancy between its maximum and minimum values for station Z?
The month with the greatest discrepancy is X.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Consider the parameter wind speed. The data consist of half-hourly measurements for station Z in year Y. Consider a table consisting of one column: the measured wind speed values in m/s. First, remove all missing measurements encoded as -9999.9. Count how many valid values are present in the table. Sum all the valid wind-speed values. Apply the following formula: total sum of values / number of valid values = result. Return this result as the output.
What is the average annual wind speed in year Y for each station?
The average annual wind speed in year Y for station Z is X m/s.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Consider the parameter precipitation. The data consist of half-hourly measurements for station Z in year Y. Consider a table consisting of one column: the measured precipitation values in millimetres (mm). First, remove all missing measurements encoded as -9999.9. Sum all the remaining values in the table. The result represents the total annual (cumulative) precipitation in mm. Return this result as the output.
What is the total annual (cumulative) precipitation in year Y for station Z?
The total annual precipitation in year Y for station Z is X mm.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Consider the parameter precipitation. The data consist of half-hourly measurements for station Z in year Y. Consider a table consisting of two columns: date (day) and measured precipitation values in millimetres (mm). First, remove all missing measurements encoded as -9999.9. For each calendar day, sum all the precipitation values of that day to obtain one daily total per day. Then, among the daily totals, find the highest value. The day corresponding to this highest daily total represents the day with the absolute maximum precipitation. Return this day as the output.
On which day of year Y did station Z record its absolute maximum daily precipitation?
The absolute maximum daily precipitation in year Y at station Z was recorded on day X.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Consider the parameter precipitation. The data consist of half-hourly measurements for station Z in year Y. Consider a table consisting of two columns: date (day) and measured precipitation values in millimetres (mm). First, remove all missing measurements encoded as -9999.9. For each calendar day, sum all the precipitation values of that day to obtain one daily total per day. Count how many days have a daily total strictly greater than 1 mm. This count represents the number of rainy days. Return this count as the output.
How many rainy days (with precipitation greater than 1 mm) were recorded in year Y at station Z?
In year Y, station Z recorded X rainy days with precipitation greater than 1 mm.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Consider the parameter temperature. The data consist of half-hourly measurements for station Z in year Y. Consider a table consisting of one column: the measured temperature values in °C (for example, column T). First, remove all missing measurements encoded as -9999.9. Count how many valid values are present in the table. Sum all the valid temperature values. Apply the following formula: total sum of values / number of valid values = result. The result represents the annual average temperature. Return this result as the output.
What is the average annual temperature in year Y for station Z?
The average annual temperature in year Y for station Z is X °C.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Consider the parameter temperature. The data consist of half-hourly measurements for station Z in year Y. Consider a table consisting of two columns: date (day and time) and measured temperature values in °C. First, remove all missing measurements encoded as -9999.9. Among the remaining values, identify the highest temperature value. Then retrieve the date corresponding to this highest value. Return this date as the output.
On which day of year Y was the maximum temperature recorded for station Z?
The maximum temperature in year Y for station Z was recorded on day X.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Consider the parameter temperature. The data consist of half-hourly measurements for station Z in year Y. Consider a table consisting of two columns: date (day and time) and measured temperature values in °C. First, remove all missing measurements encoded as -9999.9. Among the remaining values, identify the lowest temperature value. Then retrieve the date corresponding to this lowest value. Return this date as the output.
On which day of year Y was the minimum temperature recorded for station Z?
The minimum temperature in year Y for station Z was recorded on day X.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. To answer the question, identify the maximum temperature recorded in year Y for each of the 9 weather stations, then compare these values and select the highest one.
Which of the 9 weather stations recorded the highest temperature in year Y?
The weather station Z recorded the highest temperature in year Y.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. To answer the question, compute the cumulative precipitation for each weather station in year Y, then calculate the difference between the highest and the lowest cumulative values.
What is the maximum difference in cumulative precipitation among all weather stations in year Y?
The maximum difference in cumulative precipitation among the stations in year Y is X units.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. To answer the question, find the maximum and minimum wind speed recorded at each station in year Y, then identify the highest value among the maxima and the lowest value among the minima.
Which weather station recorded the highest and the lowest wind speed in year Y?
The highest wind speed was recorded at station Z1, while the lowest wind speed was recorded at station Z2 in year Y.

You are a data analyst showing data to the general public. Using daily data only, compute the daily thermal excursion (daily maximum minus daily minimum temperature) for each of the 9 weather stations, then identify the station with the largest excursion.
Which of the 9 weather stations shows the largest daily thermal excursion?
Station Z shows the largest daily thermal excursion.
